neighbours.label: a point where a relative clause is expected next: a comma or quantifier after a noun phrase ('pitchers, [which]', 'Noble, [who]', 'only one [of which]')
fire: The plant traps insects in its leaves and pitchers, which are often full of water.
I first read The Turn of the Screw by Henry James, which kept me awake all night.
The title passed to the eldest son of the duke, who inherited it at birth.
The liver makes many compounds, only one of which is cholesterol.
We stayed at a small inn near the harbor, which had a view of the boats.
The award went to Dr. Lena Ortiz, who led the vaccine trial.
He wrote three novels, the first of which became a film.
The team relied on its goalkeeper, whose saves kept them in the match.
quiet: After the long rain, the plant's leaves and pitchers were full of water.
Last winter, I read three ghost stories in a single week.
When the duke died, the title passed straight to his eldest son.
In the body, the liver makes cholesterol and many other compounds.
On our trip, we stayed at a small inn near the harbor.
This year, the award went to the doctor who led the vaccine trial.
Over ten years, he wrote three novels and a book of poems.
In the final, the team relied heavily on its goalkeeper.

notes: Card: ',' x9, ' both' x4, ' very', ' one'; the + pole's output suppresses ' which' and ' that', so the - pole promotes them. Guess: the slot just before 'which/who'. Near misses: commas after introductory phrases and in lists, where no relative clause follows.
